documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of AGM
INTIMATION FOR RESCHEDULING OF 60TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE COMPANY ON 26TH AUGUST 2026 (WEDNESDAY) AT 12:00 NOON (IST)

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its financial and operational performance for Q4 and FY 2025-26, highlighting record-high annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and highest-ever distillate yields. Management noted that borrowings have subsided significantly with a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.09, and the Board recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share. Key future capex projects include Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS and retail outlet expansion. Despite geopolitical uncertainties and logistical constraints, the company remains focused on operating efficiently and maintaining capital discipline. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its Q4 FY25 and full-year financial and operational performance, highlighting resilient capacity utilization and energy efficiency despite lower international product cracks.

demand_outlook.claim: Management stated that MS in the southern market has a clear shortfall where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern market for MS is projected to grow around 4% to 5% while national projections are at 6%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%.

demand_outlook.claim: HSD demand growth in the southern market is forecasted at 3% compared to 2.5% nationally.
demand_outlook.quote: HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has all approvals in place for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project, and project execution has started in full swing.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet endeavor has started, and commissioning will be seen during the financial year '26-'27.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the CBR project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL has full custody of approximately 1,200 acres of land for the CBR project.
capex_expansion.quote: So, about 600 acres, which was already with CPCL and another 600 acres, which was acquired in the process, both is in our possession and the pre-project activities of boundary wall construction, and all those things are almost at a big stage.

capex_expansion.claim: The new refinery capacity will be 9 million metric tons with a polypropylene petrochemical intensity of 6%.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

margins_costs.claim: The gross refining margin for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel as compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: The core GRM for quarter 4 was reported at $10.3 per barrel.
The full year GRM for 2024-25 was $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: On a full annual basis, the inventory registered a loss of $0.06 per barrel or Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

margins_costs.claim: The CPCL reported gross refining margin was $3.40 per barrel for 9M 2024-25.
The operating expenditure was Rs 945 Crore for 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved the highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 million metric tons, equivalent to 112% of installed capacity, for the financial year 2025-26.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: In quarter 4, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of installed capacity during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: In Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974 MMT, which is 113% of the installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings are INR1,900 crores and net borrowings are INR973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: Total debt stood at Rs. 3,100 crores and net worth at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024. Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Foreign exchange losses were approximately INR200 crores for the quarter and around INR350 crores for the whole year.
risks_headwinds.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge to operations.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: Product cracks in the international market reduced compared to the previous year, impacting earnings.
risks_headwinds.quote: We all know that product cracks have reduced as compared to previous year in the international market, but our endeavor to better the benchmark continues.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company incurred an exchange variation loss of Rs 122 Crore in 9M 2024-25.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects normal maintenance capex of around INR500 crores every year.
management_commitments.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

management_commitments.claim: The new LOBS unit will increase Group 2 and Group 3 capacity to 250,000 KTPA.
management_commitments.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the normal maintenance Capex will remain in the range of Rs. 200 to 250 crores.
management_commitments.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

management_commitments.claim: Without the LOBS project, normal maintenance Capex for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

management_commitments.claim: In 2025, crude unit 1 which caters to lubes will go into maintenance around August or September.
management_commitments.quote: In 2025, our refinery crude unit 1 which caters to lubes will go into maintenance around August, September.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
